summary: Array.from creates an array from an iterable or an array-like object.
documentation: Array.from creates an array from an iterable or an array-like object. With a length-only object, its mapping callback is called for each index, making it convenient to generate a bounded sequence without creating a sparse array.
inputs: An object with integer start, step and count; count is 0..20 and outputs are small integers.
caution: new Array(count).map skips unfilled slots, unlike Array.from with a mapping callback. Bound the length before accepting arbitrary external input.
scenarios: Generate tick values for a small chart axis.
Produce a numbered checklist preview starting at a chosen offset.
Build a sequence of ordered page offsets for a local paginator.
title: Generate a bounded sequence
problem: Input is {start, step, count}. Return count numbers, where item i equals start + i * step. A negative step descends; step zero repeats the start; count zero returns [].
hint: Use an array-like length object and the mapping callback’s index.
goal: Use Array.from() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
